series: The Dark Side of Once Upon a Time
title: Rumpelstiltskin: The Price of a Promise
version_scope: Brothers Grimm, final 1857 German edition, as rendered in Margaret Hunt's 1884 English translation. This is one documented literary version, not a claim about the tale's first or only form.

sources.edition: Jacob Grimm and Wilhelm Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmärchen, 7th edition (1857), vol. 1, tale 55, Rumpelstilzchen; translated by Margaret Hunt as Grimm's Household Tales, vol. 1 (London: George Bell and Sons, 1884), tale 55, Rumpelstiltskin, pp. 221–225.
sources.scope_note: The linked online transcription is Hunt's English text based on the Grimm tale; the episode identifies the German source edition and translation separately. The 1857 story ends with Rumpelstiltskin stamping his foot into the floor and wrenching it free.

narration: Before the magic, there is a threat: spin straw into gold by morning, or die. A miller boasts his daughter can spin gold. Locked in the king's room, she is rescued by a little man—first for her necklace, then her ring. The king promises to make her queen. On the third night she has nothing left, so she bargains away her first child. As queen, she bears a child; the stranger returns. Her tears win three days to guess his name. A messenger finds him dancing by a forest fire, celebrating his expected prize. She guesses correctly. In the 1857 text, he stamps one foot so deep into the floor that he must wrench it free with both hands. The queen keeps her child. The bargain ends—but what made a name powerful enough to break it?
